NOTES:
1. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (‘MCA’), inter 
alia, vide its General Circular No. 03/2025 dated 
September 22, 2025 read with other relevant 
circulars issued in this regard (collectively 
referred as ‘ MCA Circulars’), has permitted 
the companies to hold the AGM through VC/
OAVM, without the physical presence of 
members at a common venue. Further, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (‘SEBI’) 
vide Regulation 36(1) of the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015 (the ‘Listing Regulations’) has provided 
certain relaxations relating to the sending of 
Annual Report to the shareholders. 
 In compliance with the applicable provisions of 
the Companies Act, 2013 (the ‘Act’), the Listing 
Regulations and MCA Circulars, the AGM of 
the Company is being held through VC/OAVM. 
The venue of the Meeting shall be deemed 
to be the Registered Office of the Company 
situated at Ground Floor, 12A, 94, Meghdoot 
Building, Nehru Place, New Delhi-110019, and the proceedings of the AGM shall be deemed 
to be made thereat.
 To comply with the provisions of the Listing 
Regulations, the Company is also providing 
one-way live webcast of the proceedings of 
AGM which can be viewed by the Members 
on the e-voting website of the National 
Securities Depository Limited (‘NSDL ’) i.e.  
www.evoting.nsdl.com . Further, NSDL has 
also been engaged for facilitating e-voting 
to enable the Members to cast their votes 
electronically using Remote E-Voting system 
as well as E-Voting at the AGM. The procedure 
for participating in the Meeting through VC/
OAVM is explained in the notes below.
2. Pursuant to the provisions of the Act, a 
Member entitled to attend and vote at the AGM 
is entitled to appoint a proxy to attend and 
vote at the meeting on his/her behalf and the 
proxy need not be a Member of the Company. 
Since the AGM is being held pursuant to the 
framework provided in the MCA Circulars 
read with the Act and the Listing Regulations, 
through VC/OAVM, accordingly the facility for 
the appointment of Proxy by the Members will 
not be available for this AGM and hence, the 
Proxy Form, Attendance Slip and Route Map of 
AGM are not annexed to this Notice.
 However, Body Corporate Members intending  
to authorise their representatives to attend 
and vote at the AGM  pursuant to Section 113 
of the Act, are requested to  send a certified 
copy (in PDF/JPEG Format) of the relevant 
Board Resolution/Authority letter, etc. in the 
manner prescribed under Section ‘General 
Guidelines for shareholders’. 
3. Members attending the AGM through VC/
OAVM will be reckoned for the purpose of 
quorum as per Section 103 of the Act.
4. An Explanatory Statement pursuant to  Section 
102(1) of the Act setting out material facts 
relating to the special business(es) to be 
transacted at the AGM is annexed hereto. 
Further, information under Regulation 36(3) 
of the Listing Regulations and Secretarial 
Standard on General Meetings (‘SS-2’) in 
respect of the Director(s)  seeking appointment/
re-appointment at the AGM (Item Nos. 3, 5 and 
6 of the Notice) is given in Annexure-A to the 
Notice.

8. Members may note that the Income-Tax Act, 
2025 (the ‘IT Act’), mandates that dividends  
paid or distributed by a company shall 
be taxable in the hands of members. The 
Company shall therefore be required to deduct 
tax at source (‘TDS’) at the time of making the 
payment of final dividend. In order to enable 
the Company to determine the appropriate TDS 
rate as applicable, Members are requested to 
submit relevant documents, as specified in 
the below paragraphs, in accordance with the 
provisions of the IT Act.
 For resident shareholders, taxes shall be 
deducted at source under Sections 393 and 
397 of the IT Act as follows:
Members having valid 
Permanent Account 
Number (‘PAN’)10%* or as notified by the 
Government of India
Members not having 
PAN/Invalid PAN/PAN 
not linked with Aadhaar 
(Inoperative PAN)20% or as notified by the 
Government of India
 *As per Section 262 of the IT Act, every person who has 
been allotted a PAN and who is eligible to obtain Aadhaar, 
shall intimate his/her Aadhaar number to the income-
tax authority in such form and manner, as prescribed. In 
case of failure to comply with this, the PAN allotted shall 
be deemed invalid/inoperative and, such person shall be 
liable to all consequences under the IT Act and tax shall be 
deducted at the higher rates as provided in Section 397 of 
the IT Act, i.e. 20% of tax deduction at source.
 However, no TDS shall be deducted on the 
dividend payable to a resident individual if the 
total dividend to be received by them during 
FY26 does not exceed `10,000/- and also in

Page | 5  |
cases, where Members provide Form 121, 
subject to conditions specified in the IT Act. 
Resident shareholders may also submit any 
other document as prescribed under the IT Act 
to claim a lower/nil withholding tax. PAN is 
mandatory for Members providing Form 121 or 
any other document as mentioned above.
 For non-resident shareholders [including 
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)/Foreign 
Portfolio Investors (FPIs)], taxes shall be 
deducted at source in accordance with the 
provisions of Section 393 of the IT Act, at the 
rates in force. Non-resident shareholders can

subject to providing necessary documents i.e. 
copy of PAN Card, if available, No Permanent 
Establishment and Beneficial Ownership 
Declaration, Tax Residency Certificate, Form 
41, self-declaration fulfilling all conditions or 
any other document which may be required to 
avail the tax treaty benefits.

name of IEPF Authority, all shares in respect of 
which dividend has not been paid or claimed 
for 7 (Seven) consecutive years or more. In 
accordance with the aforesaid provision of 
the Act read with the Investor Education and 
Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, 
Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016, as amended, 
the Company, having adhered to the prescribed 
procedure stipulated therein, transferred all 
shares in respect of which dividend declared 
was not paid or claimed by the Members 
for 7 (Seven) consecutive years or more. 
Members are advised to visit the web-link:  
www.infoedge.in/InvestorRelations/IR_
Unpaid_Unclaimed  to ascertain details of 
shares so transferred in the name of IEPF 
Authority.
 To claim the shares transferred to IEPF 
Authority, the claimant Member is required 
to file the web based Form IEPF-5 from  
www.mca.gov.in . After filing of the said Form 
online, the claimant is required to send the 
duly filled e-form with his signature along with 
other required annexures to the RTA or the 
Company at its registered office address in 
an envelope marked as ‘Claim for  refund from 
IEPF Authority’ for initiating the verification 
for claim. The Nodal Officer of the Company 
shall verify the documents and send its report 
to the IEPF Authority, which shall upon due 
satisfaction transfer the shares to the account 
of the claimant Member.
 Further, details of the unpaid/unclaimed 
dividend (interim & final) transferred to 
the ‘Unclaimed Dividend Account’ are 
uploaded on the website of the Company at  
www.infoedge.in/InvestorRelations/IR_
Unpaid_Unclaimed .  Members willing to claim 
dividend that remain unclaimed are requested 
to correspond with the RTA or the Company.

The way to vote electronically on NSDL E-Voting 
system consists of ‘Two Steps’ which are mentioned 
below:
Step  1: Access  to NSDL  E-Voting  system
A)	 Login  method  for E-Voting  and joining  virtual  
meeting  for Individual  shareholders  holding  
securities  in demat mode
In terms of SEBI circular dated December 9, 
2020 on E-Voting facility provided by Listed Companies,  individual shareholders holding 
securities in demat mode are allowed to vote 
through their demat  account  maintained  with  
Depositories  and Depository  Participants.  
Shareholders  are advised  to update  their mobile 
number and e-mail Id in their demat accounts 
to access E-Voting facility .
Login method for individual shareholders holding 
securities in demat mode is given below:The Instructions for Remote E-Voting are as under:
Type of shareholders Login Method
Individual  Shareholders 
holding  securities  in 
demat mode with NSDL.1. For OTP based login you can click on  https://eservices.nsdl.com/SecureWeb/
evoting/evotinglogin.jsp . You will have to enter your 8-digit DP ID, 8-digit 
Client ID, PAN, Verification code and generate OTP . Enter the OTP received 
on registered e-mail id/mobile number and click on login. After successful 
authentication, you will be redirected to NSDL Depository site wherein you 
can see E-Voting page. Click on company name or E-Voting service provider 
i.e. NSDL and you will be redirected to E-Voting website of NSDL for casting 
your vote during the remote E-Voting period or joining virtual meeting & voting 
during the meeting.
2. Existing IDeAS  user can visit the e-Services website of NSDL Viz.  
eservices.nsdl.com  either on a personal computer or on a mobile. On the 
e-Services home page click on the “ Beneficial Owner ” icon under “ Login ” 
which is available under ‘IDeAS’ section, this will prompt you to enter your 
existing User ID and Password. After successful authentication, you will be 
able to see E-Voting services under Value added services. Click on “ Access to 
E-Voting ” under E-Voting services and you will be able to see E-Voting page. 
Click on company name or E-Voting service provider i.e. NSDL and you will 
be re-directed to E-Voting website of NSDL for casting your vote during the 
remote E-Voting period or joining virtual meeting & voting during the meeting.
3. If you are not registered for IDeAS e-Services, option to register is available 
at eservices.nsdl.com . Select “ Register Online for IDeAS Portal ” or click at 
eservices.nsdl.com/SecureWeb/IdeasDirectReg.jsp
4. Visit the E-Voting website of NSDL. Open web browser by typing the following 
URL: www.evoting.nsdl.com  either on a personal computer or on a mobile. 
Once the home page of E-Voting system is launched, click on the icon “ Login ” 
which is available under ‘Shareholder/ Member’ section. A new screen will 
open. You will have to enter your User ID (i.e. your sixteen digit demat account 
number hold with NSDL), Password/OTP and a Verification Code as shown 
on the screen. After successful authentication, you will be redirected to NSDL 
Depository site wherein you can see E-Voting page. Click on company name 
or E-Voting service provider i.e. NSDL  and you will be redirected to E-Voting 
website of NSDL for casting your vote during the remote E-Voting period or 
joining virtual meeting & voting during the meeting.
5.	Shareholders/Members can also download NSDL mobile app “NSDL  
Speede ” facility  by scanning  the QR code  mentioned  below for seamless voting 
experience.

About Info Edge
Building Platforms  
with Purpose
Founded in 1995 and listed since 2006, 
Info Edge is one of India’s most prominent 
consumer internet companies, with a 
market capitalisation of over ₹800 Billion 
as of July 30, 2026. For over two decades, 
the Company has pioneered the digital 
transformation of key life-stage services, 
building an enduring portfolio of category-
leading platforms across its four verticals: 
Recruitment, Real Estate, Matchmaking 
and Education.
The Company’s business is organised 
around a single objective: value-creating 
growth over the long term. Its core 
verticals sit at different stages of maturity, 
each holding strong market leadership 
in sectors where digital transformation 
continues to reshape market structures. 
Growth comes through both organic and 
inorganic routes. Organically built brands 
such as Naukri, 99acres, Jeevansathi  
and Shiksha , alongside acquisitions and 
strategic investments that enable platform 
enhancements, ecosystem development 
and capability augmentation. These are 
the foundations the Company has spent 
decades building, and the foundations on 
which it continues to build for the future.Building Beyond the Operating Businesses
Alongside its operating businesses, Info Edge channels part of its 
strong liquidity into financial investments, backing entrepreneurs 
who use technology to solve real-world problems and can scale 
into sustainable, value-creating ventures. Capital is deployed 
both directly, from the balance sheet or through wholly-owned 
subsidiaries, and through Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) 
managed by Info Edge Ventures. Through this approach, Info 
Edge has backed a wide range of companies across AI, DeepTech, 
and consumer technology domains, delivering landmark 
outcomes, most notably the public listings of Eternal Limited 
(formerly Zomato Limited) and PB Fintech Limited.
The Edge that Endures
In FY26, Info Edge showed that scale and purpose can 
coexist, deepening user engagement, accelerating AI 
adoption across all four platforms and strengthening its 
position as India’s most trusted digital ecosystem for life’s 
most important decisions. This is what building for the 
future looks like in practice: strengthening what already 
leads, while creating what comes next.
Building Smarter Platforms with AI
Info Edge’s platforms grow more intelligent with every 
interaction. Millions of daily exchanges between recruiters, 
jobseekers, buyers, families and students generate rich 
behavioural signals that continually sharpen search 
relevance, recommendations and matching accuracy. 
Backed by over a decade of investment and deep 
knowledge of AI and one of India’s largest applied AI 
labs, these proprietary datasets create a self-reinforcing 
flywheel: as participation grows, the platforms become 
more valuable and harder for competitors to replicate.

MD and CEO’s Message
Strong Foundations, 
Building Ahead
The platforms we operate, Naukri, 
99acres, Jeevansathi, and Shiksha, 
each play a meaningful role in 
some of the most important 
decisions people make in their 
lives. More than two decades 
of user trust, proprietary data, 
and deep domain expertise are 
not easily replicated. We remain 
excited about the opportunities 
ahead and committed to building 
enduring businesses that create 
lasting value for users, customers, 
employees, and shareholders.Dear Shareholders,
FY26 was a year of continued progress for Info Edge, as we 
kept building the platforms and capabilities that will shape 
our future. Despite an operating environment shaped by 
geopolitical uncertainties, rapid technological change, and 
a softer macroeconomic backdrop, the Company delivered 
a year of steady growth. Standalone billings grew 10.3% 
year-on-year to ₹31,775 Million, revenue increased 15.0% 
to ₹30,520 Million, and operating profits rose 16.9% to 
₹11,377 Million. Cash generated from operations before 
taxes stood at ₹14,693 Million, while our cash balance, 
including wholly-owned subsidiaries, reached ₹49,632 
Million at year-end. These numbers reflect a business 
that remains financially strong and operationally resilient, 
giving us the flexibility to pursue multiple opportunities 
simultaneously: strengthening our market-leading 
platforms, investing behind emerging businesses such as 
Job Hai, building AI capabilities across the organisation, 
backing high-potential founders through our venture 
capital funds, and increasing returns to shareholders.
Over the last several years, we have strengthened our 
competitive position: expanding our data assets, building 
AI capabilities, improving our products, and nurturing 
businesses we believe can become value creators. 
FY26 was the year many of these investments began to 
show up in results. Naukri is evolving from a recruitment 
marketplace into a broader talent platform. 99acres  has 
established clear traffic leadership in a market where 
that leadership has historically been difficult to achieve. 
Jeevansathi  is approaching profitability. Job Hai is 
building scale in one of India’s largest underserved 
employment segments. Our venture investing platform 
continues to support founders building the next 
generation of technology-led businesses. AI has emerged 
as one of the defining technology shifts of our time, and 
questions are understandably being asked about how 
it will reshape internet businesses and whether it could 
disrupt established platforms.
Across recruitment, real estate, matchmaking and 
education, we have spent more than two decades building 
trusted brands, large user ecosystems and proprietary 
datasets generated through billions of interactions on 
our platforms. These assets are difficult to replicate, 
and become increasingly valuable in an AI-driven 
world where high-quality data, deep domain expertise 
and strong customer relationships matter most, all of 
which our businesses possess. This conviction has 
guided our investments over the last few years, and AI 
is now embedded across all our businesses, helping us 
create better outcomes for users and customers while 
enabling us to develop new products and deepen our 
competitive advantages. 
The combination of strong market positions, proprietary 
data assets, AI capabilities, and financial strength gives 
us confidence as we look ahead, even as the operating 
environment remains dynamic and technology continues 
to evolve rapidly.
Performance Across  
Business Verticals
The global economy remained marked by geopolitical 
uncertainty and trade-related disruptions during the 
year. Despite these headwinds, India continued to 
demonstrate resilience, supported by strong domestic 
demand and structural fundamentals. While international 
developments may have implications for recruitment, 
real estate and Shiksha Abroad, our exposure remains 
limited due to our predominantly India-focused business 
portfolio. As one of India’s leading digital classifieds 
companies, we remain well positioned to benefit from 
India’s continued digital adoption and long-term growth.
Recruitment Business:  
Sustained Leadership and Strategic 
Expansion
Navigating a Measured Hiring Environment
FY26 saw a more measured hiring environment, with 
employers cautious and selective, particularly in IT 
services. Within GCCs, smaller and mid-sized centres 
continued to hire actively while larger GCCs moved more 
deliberately. Non-IT hiring moderated after a period of 
strong growth, likely reflecting near-term caution rather 
than a structural shift in demand.
An underappreciated dynamic is the role of workforce 
attrition in sustaining hiring volumes. Attrition has 
remained elevated, and companies have progressively 
reduced bench strength to manage costs, increasing 
reliance on external hiring. What matters for Naukri is 
gross hiring demand rather than net headcount addition, 
and on that measure, the market remains active. 
As companies replace attrition and step up growth 
investments, we expect hiring activity to strengthen further.
Premium Hiring: A Growing Segment  
Where Naukri is Gaining Share
One of the more significant structural trends in Indian 
recruitment over the past two years has been the rapid 
growth of premium hiring, driven by demand for AI and 
ML engineers, data scientists, technology architects, and 
other emerging-technology specialists who command 
higher compensation and disproportionate attention 
from recruiters.
We are actively gaining market share in the premium 
hiring market, and continue to invest in expanding 
our offering here. Alongside Naukri, through iimjobs, 
Hirist, Naukri Top Tier and PremiumX, we now offer a 
comprehensive suite of products serving leadership, 
management and specialised technology hiring 
segments, positioning premium hiring as a durable 
growth engine for our recruitment business. This is a 
high-value part of the market, and our growing presence 
here supports both revenue growth and revenue per client 
improvement over time.

Mid-Segment Hiring:  
High Market Share, AI-Powered Growth
Naukri’s leadership in the mid-market hiring segment 
remains strong, supported by the depth of our resume 
database, long-standing client relationships, and the 
network effects inherent in the platform. While volume 
growth in this segment has moderated alongside broader 
hiring trends, our focus is on growing revenue per hire 
through a set of value-added offerings that deepen our 
relationship with recruiters and employers. 
Naukri is turning its AI and data capabilities into 
standalone enterprise revenue streams. Talent Pulse, 
our AI-powered talent intelligence platform, now serves 
over 600 paid customers, ranging from large enterprises 
to smaller organisations, helping them benchmark 
compensation, assess talent availability, evaluate 
employer branding, and plan their workforce with AI-driven  
insights. Together with executive intelligence, these 
products are expanding Naukri’s addressable market into 
talent intelligence and strategic workforce planning.
AI-Rex, our agentic AI-powered recruitment talent sourcing 
platform, is now live with over 4,000 enterprise customers 
and recruitment firms, with more than 10% already 
converted to paid clients. Hiring mandates through AI-Rex 
grew 3.7x between February and June 2026, and adoption 
now spans IT, BFSI, sales, finance, healthcare, BPO and 
core engineering, among others. These offerings are 
helping expand our role from a hiring platform to a broader 
talent solutions partner, creating opportunities to deepen 
customer engagement and increase revenue per client.
Expanding the Jobseeker Base
Naukri today hosts approximately 118 Million resumes, 
with around 25,000 new profiles added daily for the 
quarter ending June 30, 2026. This jobseeker base is the 
foundation of Naukri’s value to recruiters: more jobseekers 
attract more employers, which in turn attracts more 
jobseekers, and this flywheel is the core reason Naukri’s 
lead over competitors has widened. The transition to 
Naukri 360, a shift to a self-serve, online-first model, has 
been a defining strategic move. Naukri 360 now includes 
an AI-powered suite of career services for candidates: 
Neo, the jobseeker agent, provides guided career 
navigation and job matching; AI Resume Maker helps 
candidates build stronger profiles; and AI Mock Interview 
Prep offers personalised practice sessions and feedback 
ahead of real conversations with recruiters. Together, 
these have driven the online revenue mix from 27% to 54% 
over the last 18 months. Approximately 13 Million monthly 
active users now use the platform, with a paid conversion 
rate of approximately 2.6% as of June 2026 that has 
grown meaningfully, leaving significant headroom ahead. 
Premium subscriptions for these AI tools are contributing 
to stronger revenue growth within our jobseeker 
revenue pool.Real Estate Business:  
Traffic Leadership, an Inflection Point, and 
the Next Phase of Growth
FY26 was a standout year for 99acres. Seven quarters 
ago, we were in a three-way contest for traffic leadership. 
Today, 99acres is the clear and established leader: web 
traffic time share grew from 32% in June 2024 to 51% by 
March 2026, with app traffic share at 56% overall and 70% 
on iOS, a gain of roughly 0.5 to 1 percentage point every 
month over the past 12 to 18 months. Across key markets, 
99acres is now the leader in traffic and is increasingly in 
supply and revenue as well. Supply momentum remained 
strong, with over 1.3 Million total listings on the platform.
In residential resale, our strongest segment, daily fresh 
supply is up more than 40% over the past two years, supply 
share has crossed 50%, and response growth has nearly 
doubled, while rental and commercial are also seeing 
faster growth in response. Residential resale is a business 
defined by network effects. More listings attract more 
buyers, more buyers attract more sellers, and the quality 
and depth of the marketplace compound with every cycle. 
In many global markets, online real estate platforms have 
evolved into larger businesses than online job boards, 
reflecting the scale and depth of the property ecosystem. 
As urbanisation deepens and the resale market matures 
in India over the coming years, we believe 99acres is well 
positioned to capture this long-term opportunity and 
continue growing ahead of the broader market.
In new projects, a market estimated at ₹50-55 Billion 
today and historically dominated by Meta and Google for 
developer advertising spend, 99acres is now making early 
inroads. Response growth improved year-on-year in FY26, 
compared to a flattish trend in FY25. We recently launched 
99Shorts in NCR, an Instagram-style short-video feed 
for real estate project discovery, with expansion to other 
major cities planned in the coming year. The addressable 
market for new homes advertising is expected to grow 
over the next several years, supported by steady primary 
development and the continuing shift of developer 
advertising spend online. If we execute well, new homes 
can become a sizeable revenue pool for us.FY26 billings grew 10.3% to ₹4,971 Million, while revenue 
grew 18.8% to ₹4,881 Million. 99acres has secured 
traffic leadership, which is by far the hardest step in this 
business, and supply, responses, and revenue are now 
following in that order. This is a difficult category to win 
and our consistent execution here has played a major 
role in establishing a decisive lead over many quarters. 
With the intense investment phase behind us, we expect 
operating leverage to play out and growth to accelerate, 
with a near-term goal of 60% web traffic time share as the 
fundamentals increasingly favour us. Taken together, our 
position in residential resale and our early progress in new 
homes give us confidence that real estate can become 
one of our largest businesses over time.
Matchmaking Business:  
Growing Faster and Approaching 
Profitability 
FY26 was a year of consistent progress for Jeevansathi. 
Billings grew 28.5% to ₹1,424 Million, revenues increased 
25.9% to ₹1,383 Million, and the business generated 
₹147 Million in cash from operations. Jeevansathi is 
now the number one matrimonial site in the Hindi belt, 
where it holds over 45% profile share and leads by daily 
active users. 
We now own 100% of Aisle, our serious-intent dating 
platform. Aisle grew billings by 29.7% in FY26. Arike, our 
Malayalam-focused app, grew at over 40% and leads its 
segment. Jeevansathi, complemented by Aisle, is now 
growing faster than the broader matchmaking market. 
Together, the combined matchmaking portfolio reported 
₹1,817 Million in billings in FY26, growing 28.7% year-
on-year, with combined operating losses reducing by 
49.7% to ₹150 Million. We expect the combined portfolio 
to breakeven in FY27 and to sustain healthy, profitable 
growth from there.
AI is central to this business. Recommendations, 
matching, and pricing at Jeevansathi are now fully AI-
driven. This has led to measurable improvements in profile 
acceptance rates, two-way chat frequency, and overall 
user satisfaction. These are the leading indicators of paid 
conversion, and they are moving in the right direction.
NaukriGulf: From Indian Diaspora Platform 
to Regional Hiring Platform
NaukriGulf began as a platform for the Indian professional 
diaspora in the Gulf. It has since grown into one of the 
leading hiring platforms in the Middle East, serving a 
diverse employer base across multiple industries and 
geographies in the region.
The business continues to grow profitably, demonstrating 
the depth and resilience of the regional recruitment market 
and providing a strong platform for continued expansion.
Job Hai: Building for Blue-Collar Hiring
Job Hai is one of our most important long-term 
investments, and FY26 marked the year it moved from 
early-stage validation to platform establishment at scale. 
The blue-collar hiring market in India is large, fast-
growing, and largely underserved by organised technology 
platforms. Unlike white-collar hiring, this is inherently a 
high-volume, high-frequency business, with employers 
numbering in the millions and hiring cycles repeating often 
given elevated attrition. This dynamic is best illustrated 
by a blue-collar recruitment platform in China, which now 
serves employers at a scale and frequency few consumer 
internet businesses reach. India’s blue-collar workforce 
is significantly larger, and if we execute well, we believe 
there is a meaningful long-term opportunity for Job Hai. 
Job Hai’s opportunity is to build for this segment what 
Naukri built for white-collar hiring: a trusted, data-rich, 
high-frequency platform that becomes the default for both 
employers and jobseekers.
The platform has now reached 18 Million jobseekers, 
130,000+ live jobs, and coverage across 640+ cities 
and 45+ job categories. JobHai is the market leader in 
Delhi NCR, the largest blue-collar hiring market in India, 
and is building the playbook for expansion into Mumbai, 
Bengaluru, and other key metros. The monetisation model 
spans job postings, database access, job boost, assisted 
hiring, and WhatsApp-based outreach, serving SMBs, 
enterprise clients, and recruitment consultants. We expect 
JobHai to be a significant contributor to group revenue in 
the medium to long term.
Financial Performance
Standalone recruitment billings grew 10.0% to ₹23,743 
Million, while revenue grew 13.8% to ₹22,559 Million. The 
business delivered an operating profit of ₹12,772 Million, 
up 14.4% year-on-year, with an operating margin of 56.6%, 
and generated ₹15,127 Million in cash from operations, 
12.5% higher than the prior year.

Education Business: Adapting 
to a Changing Landscape
Shiksha operated in a challenging environment in FY26. 
AI-generated search summaries and conversational 
interfaces are reshaping how students discover 
information online, compressing organic traffic across 
education platforms. At the same time, the study-abroad 
segment has been hit hard by growing negativity around 
immigration in key destination markets and by tightening 
visa policies. Taken together, we expect revenue in this 
business to decline in the near term.
For the year, billings grew 0.8% to ₹1,637 Million, revenues 
increased 12.9% to ₹1,698 Million, and the business 
delivered ₹131 Million of operating profit and ₹216 Million 
in cash from operations. Shiksha remains profitable and 
cash-generative, and we are progressing quickly to pivot. 
The core opportunity ahead is counselling at scale: AI 
now lets us deliver personalised guidance to far more 
students, at a fraction of the cost of a purely human-
led model. We are shifting towards a counselling-led 
business anchored in direct, high-intent user engagement 
rather than organic search traffic and diversifying our 
study abroad mix towards the UK, UAE, and continental 
Europe. While the near-term revenue outlook is subdued, 
we believe counselling at scale can open up a materially 
larger opportunity for Shiksha over time.

of Investment
Several years ago, we made a deliberate decision to build

businesses. We invested approximately ₹700 Million in AI 
in FY26, expected to rise to approximately ₹1.5 Billion in 
FY27. This spending spans talent, compute infrastructure, 
our data factory, and the development of our own small 
language models tuned to our domains. At the heart 
of these investments is our data factory. Two decades 
of interactions across Naukri, 99acres, Jeevansathi Looking Ahead

In recruitment, we remain focused on deepening client

In matchmaking, Jeevansathi and Aisle together remain

Across all our businesses, our greatest asset is our

on Naukri, profile acceptance rates have gone up on

We are embedding AI into customer and user workflows,

Alongside AI-Rex, our Data Products suite and Talent

intelligence partner, and PremiumX is deepening our 
position in premium hiring.
More important is the competitive point: we are not being 
displaced by AI in recruitment; we are becoming the 
platform through which AI reaches the industry. Users 
are moving toward platforms with richer, more structured 
data, not away from them. Businesses with trusted brands, 
proprietary data, and strong user ecosystems benefit from 
this transition rather than being threatened by it.
More broadly, here is how we think about AI: Using 
AI tools for productivity and applying AI to improve 
individual features are, in our view, table stakes. They 
are the minimum required to stay in the game, and 
every serious internet company will do them. The bigger 
opportunity, where we are focusing our energy, sits in 
three areas. The first is frugal AI. Since we serve AI to 
hundreds of millions of users, the ability to run our own 
small language models cost-effectively at scale is a 
meaningful advantage. The second is our data factory 
and the proprietary datasets we have built over two 
decades. The third is using AI to create new products 
and experiences. Together, these pillars position us to 
create new businesses, expand into adjacent markets 
and overtime help us increase our addressable market 
and further improve our unit economics.Financial and  
Strategic Investments
Capital allocation has always been an important part 
of how we think about value creation at Info Edge. Over 
the years, we have sought to balance investments in our 
operating businesses with long-term financial investing 
in early-stage companies, while maintaining a strong 
balance sheet and delivering returns to shareholders.
Our investment philosophy is straightforward: identifying 
exceptional founders early, investing before consensus 
forms, and staying invested longer than most. This 
approach has produced substantial value over nearly two 
decades, most visibly in Eternal and PB Fintech, which 
together demonstrate what patient, early-stage investing 
can deliver when it is given time to compound.
Today, our financial investment portfolio spans 
135 companies across AI, DeepTech, and consumer 
technology, with a total deployed capital of approximately 
₹49 Billion, currently valued at approximately ₹413 Billion. 
We have been particularly active in AI and DeepTech since 
2020, investing ahead of the broader market wave. While 
these are still early days for many of these businesses, 
intermediate results have been encouraging: follow-on 
rounds from marquee institutional investors, government 
programme selections, and early revenue traction give us 
confidence in the direction of travel.
We remain focused on the same things that have always 
guided our investing: quality of founders, discipline on 
entry, and the patience to let compounding do its work.

Business Verticals Review
Building How India Hires
Anchored by its flagship platform Naukri, Info Edge’s recruitment vertical 
operates India’s largest jobs marketplace, strengthening its leadership even 
as talent dynamics continue to evolve. 
₹22,559 Mn
Standalone Revenue
118 Mn
Resume Database*56.6 %
Standalone Operating PBT Margin
146,000+
Unique Billed Customers
^YoY change
*For the recruitment of India B2B business, as of June 30, 2026₹23,743 Mn
Standalone BillingsIndia’s employment landscape is undergoing a 
fundamental shift. Digital adoption, the growth of GCCs, 
sectoral expansion across, healthcare, retail, education, 
real estate along with rise in demand for skilled 
professionals with expertise in AI, data science, amongst 
others, and the formalisation of blue- and grey-collar roles 
are reshaping how the country hires. Naukri has evolved 
with these changes, maturing from India’s most trusted 
white-collar recruitment platform into a comprehensive 
talent solutions ecosystem, built through sustained 
organic investment and strategic acquisitions. AI now 
runs through the platform end to end. For employers, 
AI-powered recommendations and matching, smart job 
alerts, automated shortlisting, ATS integrations, and 
recruiter productivity tools enable better matches and 
faster hiring.
AI-Rex, an agentic AI recruitment platform, enables talent 
sourcing automation for enterprises—from job mandate 
intake to candidate shortlisting—meaningfully reducing 
time-to-hire. Info Edge is also leveraging its proprietary 
data to build AI-powered talent intelligence products, 
such as Talent Pulse, offering enterprises actionable 
insights on salaries, hiring trends, and workforce 
planning. For jobseekers, AI tools help build stronger 
resumes, practise mock interviews and discover the right 
roles—now supported by Neo, an AI job agent offering 
real-time alerts, intelligent discovery and auto-apply. 
Naukri’s reach now extends to over 146,000 corporate 
clients including enterprise customers, GCCs, recruitment 
agencies etc., while its resume database has grown to  
118 Million hosted profiles, reflecting strong 
engagement and trust on both sides of the marketplace. 
The recruitment ecosystem is organised around four 
complementary categories.Recruitment India B2B
The core of the business, led by Naukri, holds a leadership 
position in white-collar hiring, serving over 146,000 
corporate clients. It spans across the premium segment 
(above ₹30 Lakh CTC), mid segment (₹5–30 Lakh CTC) 
and value segment (less than ₹5 CTC), supported by a 
portfolio of specialised platforms and enterprise tools:
• Naukri  along with specialised platforms, iimjobs, 
and Hirist  serve the fast-growing premium segment. 
iimjobs primarily caters to senior management and 
leadership hiring, while Hirist is an exclusive platform 
for premium technology talent. Naukri TopTier , 
offered as part of the Core Naukri platform, provides a 
differentiated, invite-only experience for premium job 
seekers. PremiumX , launched in FY26, further extends 
the Company’s premium offerings. 
• Naukri Campus  supports fresher hiring for the digital-
first generation.
• AmbitionBox  offers company reviews and salary 
insights, helping candidates make informed decisions.
• Zwayam  is an AI-powered enterprise recruitment 
automation platform that digitises the end-to-end 
hiring process.
• DoSelect  is a technical assessment platform used by 
clients to evaluate and hire tech talent.
• AI-Rex  is Naukri’s agentic AI platform, enabling end-to-
end hiring workflows from mandate intake to candidate 
shortlisting, to reduce time-to-hire.
• Talent Pulse and Executive Intelligence turn 
proprietary data into AI-powered talent insights on 
salaries, branding, movement and workforce planning.₹15,127 Mn
Cash Flow from Operations ^12.5%
Recruitment
Naukri’s billings remain well diversified across 
tech, IT services and BPM (27.1%), GCCs (17.3%), 
recruitment consultants (26.4%) and other sectors 
(29.2%),  underscoring its relevance across company 
sizes, industries and geographies.
The Recruitment B2B businesses accounted for 86.7% 
of total recruitment billings in FY26.
Candidate and Jobseeker  
Services (B2C)
Naukri’s Jobseeker Services comprise Naukri 360, 
Naukri FastForward, and Naukri Minis, offering  
AI-powered career guidance, resume building, interview 
preparation, an Neo- AI job agent for personalised job 
discovery, and bite-sized engaging content, while driving 
user engagement and monetisation.
The business accounted for 7.4% of total recruitment 
billings in FY26.
NaukriGulf
Beyond India, NaukriGulf offers localised recruitment 
solution across the six GCC countries of the Middle East, 
with primary focus on UAE, having grown from a focus 
on the Indian diaspora into a leading regional platform 
serving diverse nationalities. 
NaukriGulf business accounted for 5.3% of total 
recruitment billings in FY26.
Job Hai
Alongside Naukri’s value segment, Job Hai serves the 
blue- and grey-collar workforce across India’s large, 
fragmented and rapidly formalising market across 
multiple sectors. Structurally underpenetrated, it 
represents a significant long-term opportunity that the 
platform was purpose-built to serve.
Job Hai is building momentum and is well positioned to 
expand the Company’s presence in the blue- and grey-
collar hiring segment. By building for the future—investing 
ahead of shifting workforce needs across AI, premium 
hiring and new recruitment segments—Naukri continues 
to help Indian enterprises hire smarter and faster at scale, 
while laying the foundations for its next phase of growth.

India’s real estate sector carried strong momentum 
through FY26, with the office market scaling new highs 
and the residential market extending its post-pandemic 
upcycle. As property discovery moves online, digital 
platforms have become critical enablers of a more 
transparent, informed transaction experience. For 
99acres, FY26 was a year of disciplined execution against 
a multi-year transformation, progressing from competing 
among the top three players to clear leadership in traffic.^18.8%                           
Real Estate
Extending Market Leadership
99acres now leads online real estate in web traffic time 
share at 51% (Similar Web, March 31, 2026), up from 
around 32%, seven quarters ago, and is now ahead 
across nearly every major city in traffic, supply and 
customers. On mobile, it commands 56% of app traffic 
time share and 70% on iOS.
Two Business Areas
The secondary business (resale across residential and 
commercial) performed well, with residential resale 
supply share crossing 50% and response growth nearly 
doubling. The primary business (new projects and 
homes) remains a key strategic priority, with response 
growth reaching 30% YoY. The platform also carries 
wide-ranging rental listings across residential and 
commercial categories.
Content, AI, and Reach
The business continues to invest in high-quality content, 
an improved interface and AI across content generation, 
lead conversion and customer service, deepening 
new-homes engagement through 99Shorts. Info Edge 
believes the future of real estate in India is digital-first, 
and by building on its traffic leadership and investing 
ahead of the shift towards new homes, 99acres is well 
positioned to make that future more accessible, informed 
and trustworthy.

Aisle

more intentional audience: those seeking committed 
relationships rather than casual encounters. Aisle has

generation, including Arike (Malayali), Anbe (Tamil), 
Neetho (Telugu) and Neene (Kannada). Arike has 
established clear leadership in the Malayalam dating 
segment, growing consistently at 40%+ YoY. Making 
Aisle free for women has further strengthened platform 
engagement and match quality.
AI Across the Portfolio
AI is now embedded across both platforms, with 
recommendations, matching and pricing fully AI-driven, 
improving profile acceptance, two-way chats and user 
satisfaction. The platform is leveraging GenAI and data 
science capabilities to make partner search simpler, 
faster, and more relevant.
By building for the future—investing in trusted, 
community-aware experiences and AI-led discovery 
across both matrimony and dating—Info Edge’s 
matchmaking vertical is well positioned to serve India’s 
changing relationship landscape.

Operating PBTShiksha has evolved from a simple information hub

Adapting to a Changing  
Search Landscape

platforms like Shiksha. In response, the business is

generation model towards comprehensive counselling 
and marketing services—that deepens its role across the 
student journey. This includes strengthening domestic 
counselling, improving enquiry-to-application conversion, 
deploying AI-driven voice bots and building more 
diversified, resilient revenue streams.
By evolving from information provider to trusted 
counselling partner and investing in AI, Shiksha is building 
for the future, positioning itself to capture the sustained 
growth of India’s higher-education market.

makes strategic investments in businesses 
that strengthen and complement its core 
platforms, building today the portfolio that 
will create tomorrow’s returns.
Investment Philosophy
Driven by Info Edge’s commitment to driving purposeful 
progress, the Company has adopted a focused 
investment strategy centred on India’s fast-growing 
startup ecosystem. It prioritises early-stage investments, 
primarily in Seed, Pre-Series A and Series A rounds, 
aiming to be the first institutional investor in these 
ventures. The Company’s investment philosophy is 
grounded in backing technology-led or technology-
enabled solutions that address local challenges across 
diverse sectors. First cheques are typically smaller in 
size, with an expected holding period of 10 years or 
longer. Follow-on commitments are contingent on the 
investee’s strong business performance and equitable 
treatment of minority shareholders.
Investment Strategy and Structure
Info Edge aims to partner with these businesses through 
their lifecycle, as they grow, stabilise, and eventually 
achieve a public market presence or undergo a strategic 
acquisition. The Company formalised its investment 
framework in FY20 by establishing a portfolio of AIFs 
that invest in early-stage Indian startups across sectors 
like AI, DeepTech and ConsumerTech, amongst others 
such as SaaS and FinTech. During FY26, this platform 
was extended further with the launch of three new 
schemes: IE Venture Investment Fund III, which continues 
to back early-stage companies across consumer internet 
 For further details on Investments refer to the Management Discussion and Analysis on Page 95platforms, B2B marketplaces, SaaS products, AI and  
AI-enabled platforms, and emerging technologies;  
B8 Fund I, a growth-stage scheme focusing on 
technology-enabled companies in India; and A88 Fund I, 
focused on deep technology. In building this layered 
investment platform, Info Edge is building future value 
for all its stakeholders: founders who gain a committed 
long-term partner, shareholders who benefit from 
diversified long-term value creation, and the wider 
innovation ecosystem in which the next generation of 
Indian companies is being built.

Info Edge’s AI journey has evolved through three 
distinct phases.
The first phase focused on building foundational AI 
capabilities, including semantic search, recommendation 
engines and intelligent matching. The second phase

real estate and matchmaking through deep learning, 
personalisation and predictive intelligence. The current 
phase  is centred on Generative AI and Agentic AI, enabling 
conversational interfaces, talent sourcing automation and 
autonomous decision support across customer journeys.
Today, AI is embedded across every major business of 
the Company. Rather than functioning as a standalone 
technology initiative, it powers search, recommendations, 
matching, content generation, pricing, talent sourcing 
automation and enterprise intelligence across 
multiple platforms.

At Info Edge, building for the future also means operating with ecological 
responsibility. The Company continues to integrate sustainable practices across 
its operations, recognising that long-term business resilience and environmental 
stewardship operate in tandem. Its environmental approach is focused on improving 
energy efficiency, responsibly managing electronic waste, increasing renewable 
energy consumption, reducing emissions and creating greener workplaces. 
Energy Efficiency
Info Edge continues to adopt efficient technologies 
and processes to reduce energy consumption across 
its operations.Responsible E-Waste Management
As a digital-first organisation, responsible management 
of electronic waste remains an important environmental 
priority. Info Edge has policies in place for the responsible 
disposal and recycling of electronic and battery waste, 
helping reduce the environmental hazards associated  
with such waste.
Renewable Energy Adoption
Info Edge continues to move towards cleaner energy 
sources and reducing dependence on fossil fuels by 
increasing renewable energy use across its operations. 
The Company’s rooftop solar installation at its corporate

by reducing dependence on grid electricity and lowering 
greenhouse gas emissions.Emissions Management
Info Edge continues to monitor and manage its 
emissions footprint. The Company has recorded a

Management  
Discussion and  
Analysis
FY26 was marked by heightened global uncertainty. 
Resurfacing tariff pressures, the continuing Russia–Ukraine 
war, intermittent India–Pakistan tensions, and escalating 
instability in the Middle East contributed to a more cautious 
operating environment, alongside evolving risks around 
inflation, interest rates, trade flows and supply chain 
realignments. At the same time, rapid advances in Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) emerged as a defining structural shift, 
creating significant opportunities to enhance products, user 
engagement and productivity while accelerating technological 
disruption across industries.
Under the circumstances, Info Edge delivered resilient 
performance in FY26, supported by the strength of its 
diversified digital portfolio, healthy profitability and robust 
cash generation. The recruitment business continued to grow 
steadily while maintaining industry -leading margins, and the 
Company’s non -recruitment businesses gained market share, 
sustained growth momentum and collectively generated 
positive cash flows from operations. The Company continued 
to embed AI across its platforms while launching new AI -native 
products, and its investment portfolio created long -term 
shareholder value as major investee companies, including 
Eternal Limited (Eternal) and PB Fintech Limited (PB Fintech), 
scaled their businesses and improved profitability.

Business Environment
The Global Economy
According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the global GDP is projected to grow by 3.0% in CY26 and 3.4% in 
CY27, compared with 3.5% in CY25, reflecting a moderation in growth as businesses and consumers adjust to a more 
challenging macroeconomic environment. Inflation is expected to remain above long -term averages, although on a gradual 
easing trajectory.
While the baseline outlook remains stable, risks from 
geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation, commodity 
price volatility and tighter financial conditions continue 
to pose challenges to global growth. At the same time, 
rapid advances in AI are beginning to reshape business 
models and investment priorities across industries. For 
digital platform businesses such as Info Edge, these global 
developments influence operating conditions through three 
principal channels. First, hiring demand in export -oriented 
sectors, particularly information technology services, 
remains linked to global economic activity. Second, the 
overseas education market is influenced by changing visa 
policies, student mobility and geopolitical developments. 
Third, global capital flows and investor sentiment continue 
to affect technology valuations and the Company’s 
investment portfolio. 
Despite these headwinds, Info Edge’s diversified business 
portfolio demonstrated resilience during FY26. The 
recruitment business navigated a measured hiring 
environment while sustaining profitable growth. NaukriGulf 
benefitted from healthy hiring activity across the Middle 
East for most of the year, with moderation towards the end 
of the year owing to regional conflicts. While Shiksha’s 
Study Abroad business remained impacted by tighter visa 
norms in key destination markets, the Company’s major 
listed investments continued to scale profitably and create 
long -term shareholder value.The Indian Economy
India continued to be one of the fastest -growing major 
economies during FY26, supported by resilient domestic 
demand, sound macroeconomic fundamentals, and 
continued public investment in infrastructure and 
digitalisation. While economic growth moderated from 
the exceptionally strong levels of the previous year, it 
remained well ahead of most large economies. The IMF 
projects India’s real GDP growth at 6.4% in FY26 and 6.7% 
in FY27, reflecting the country’s favourable long -term 
growth outlook.
The operating environment during the year remained 
influenced by global uncertainties, including geopolitical 
tensions, elevated commodity prices, and a softer external 
demand environment. Nevertheless, continued urbanisation, 
formalisation of the economy, rising household incomes, 
expanding digital adoption and favourable demographics 
continue to support long -term growth across India’s 
consumption and services sectors.India’s Digital & AI Transformation 
India’s digital economy continued to expand rapidly 
during FY26, supported by one of the world’s largest 
internet user bases, affordable mobile data, widespread 
smartphone adoption and continued investments in digital 
public infrastructure. Digital technologies are increasingly 
transforming how individuals access employment, 
housing, education, financial services, healthcare and 
commerce, creating significant long -term opportunities 
for platform businesses.
The country’s digital transformation continues to be 
underpinned by strong policy support. Over the past decade, 
the Digital India programme has accelerated internet 
connectivity, digital inclusion and the adoption of digital 
public infrastructure. Platforms such as Unified Payments 
Interface (UPI), Aadhaar, DigiLocker and BharatNet have 
significantly reduced friction across the economy while 
improving access to digital services. As digital adoption 
deepens, India’s digital economy is expected to become an 
increasingly important contributor to the country’s overall 
economic growth over the coming decade.
Alongside this digital transformation, AI is emerging as 
the next structural driver of productivity and innovation. 
Enterprises across sectors are increasingly integrating 
AI into customer engagement, decision -making, software 
development and business operations. India is well-
positioned to participate in this transition, supported by a 
vibrant technology ecosystem, one of the world’s largest 
pools of digital talent, and a rapidly expanding startup 
landscape. The country today hosts more than 2,100 
Global Capability Centres (GCCs), which are increasingly 
undertaking high -value work across engineering, product 
development, data science and AI. Government initiatives 
such as the IndiaAI Mission are further strengthening 
the country’s AI ecosystem by expanding compute 
infrastructure, promoting indigenous AI research, 
improving access to high -quality datasets, supporting 
startup innovation and investing in talent development. 
The convergence of digital infrastructure, AI innovation, a 
strong technology talent pool and supportive public policy 
is creating a favourable environment for technology-led 
businesses, positioning India as one of the most attractive 
long -term digital growth markets globally.Implications for Info Edge
The long -term structural trends shaping the global and 
Indian economies map directly to Info Edge’s businesses. 
Formalisation of employment, expansion of GCCs, and 
growing demand for specialised talent in AI, data science, 
cybersecurity and product engineering continue to expand 
the addressable market for the Company’s recruitment 
platforms led by Naukri , while the continued formalisation of 
blue - and grey -collar employment strengthens the long -term 
opportunity for Job Hai. Beyond recruitment, increasing 
digital discovery and transparency support 99acres , rising 
consumer trust in digital platforms benefits Jeevansathi , 
and India’s large and aspirational student population 
underpins long -term demand for higher education guidance 
through Shiksha . Across all businesses, AI acts as both an 
opportunity and a catalyst for change—a theme examined

Business Structure
Info Edge's business segments are organised around a single objective: value-creating growth 
over the long term. The Company drives this through investments in its operating businesses, 
which strengthen competitiveness and create synergies across the existing portfolio. At the 
same time, Info Edge maintains a strong liquidity position, holding sufficient cash and cash 
equivalents, to safeguard its core operations from financial risk. To make better use of this 
cash, the Company also channels a part of it into financial investments, backing startups led 
by committed entrepreneurs who use technology to solve real-world problems and have the 
potential to scale into sustainable, long term value-creating ventures.
The Business Portfolio
Strategically, the business comprises two portfolios: operating businesses and financial investments.Financial Investments
Info Edge follows a hybrid approach here, deploying capital both directly from Balance Sheet and through Wholly-Owned 
Subsidiaries and through Alternate Investment Funds (AIFs) This lets the Company back promising early-stage startups 
without diverting focus from its core operations. Over time, this segment has matured into a structured platform built on 
two avenues:
Operating Businesses
The core verticals—Recruitment, Real Estate, Matchmaking, 
and Education—sit at different stages of maturity, each 
holding strong market leadership in dynamic sectors 
where digital transformation continues to reshape market 
structures. Growth comes through both organic and 
inorganic routes. Organically grown brands include Naukri, 
Job Hai, etc. in Recruitment, 99acres in Real Estate, 
Jeevansathi in Matchmaking, and Shiksha in Education, 
with priorities centred on expanding services, enhancing 
user experience, and building new revenue streams while 
defending category leadership. Inorganically, growth is supported by strategic investments 
and acquisitions like Zwayam, DoSelect and Aisle, enabling 
platform enhancements, ecosystem development, and 
capability augmentation across vertical and horizontal 
expansion, market consolidation, and new capabilities. 
Each business, along with its related investments, is run 
by an independent, empowered team with strong domain 
leadership, operating with autonomy to drive innovation 
while central functions, Finance, Legal, HR, and IT, provide 
governance and ensure alignment with group-level policy.Direct Investments through Balance Sheet 
and through Wholly-Owned Subsidiaries
Typically directed at early-stage startups with long-term 
value potential, this route has already delivered notable 
outcomes, including the successful listings of Eternal and 
PB Fintech.Investments through AIF
Capital is also channelled through AIF schemes managed 
by Info Edge Ventures and its investment management 
team. These funds are managed by experienced investment 
professionals under a robust risk-management framework 
and are focused on generating long-term value through 
disciplined capital allocation. The Company’s investments 
are currently channelled through the following schemes:

Market Overview
India’s recruitment market continued to demonstrate 
resilience during FY26 despite a measured hiring 
environment. While macroeconomic uncertainty, 
geopolitical developments and a cautious spending 
environment saw moderated recruitment activity across 
certain sectors, the long -term fundamentals of India’s 
employment market remained robust.
Hiring activity during FY26 remained measured as 
organisations balanced cost discipline with selective 
investments in growth. While hiring in IT services continued 
to remain subdued for much of the year, demand across 
several non -IT sectors demonstrated greater endurance. 
The Naukri JobSpeak Index reflected these trends through 
the year, with hiring activity stabilising after the moderation 
witnessed over the previous two years and gradually 
improving across several sectors towards the latter part 
of FY26.
Hiring remained particularly stable across GCCs, 
hospitality, healthcare, retail, education and real estate, 
while demand for professionals with expertise in AI, data 
science, cybersecurity and product engineering continued 
to grow significantly faster than the broader market. 
Hiring momentum also broadened geographically, with 
Tier II cities continuing to gain prominence as enterprises 
expanded operations beyond traditional metropolitan hubs.
Structural Drivers
A defining characteristic of India’s recruitment market is 
that hiring demand is influenced not only by employment 
growth but also by workforce mobility. Employee attrition Recruitment 
Recruitment is Info Edge’s largest and most profitable business, and has been the cornerstone of 
the Company’s growth for more than two decades. Beyond being its principal revenue and profit 
generator, it has provided the financial strength to invest in technology, new businesses and 
one of India’s leading internet investment portfolios. Today, the business operates one of India’s 
most comprehensive talent hiring ecosystems, connecting recruiters and jobseekers across the 
entire hiring value chain through enterprise hiring solutions, specialised recruitment platforms, 
AI-powered products, jobseeker services, recruitment workflow software, skill assessment 
solutions, geographic expansion and the value segment.Business Review
Businesses Under Direct Management in the Standalone Entity
continues to generate significant recruitment activity 
even during periods of moderate economic growth, as 
organisations increasingly rely on external hiring to replace 
attrition, acquire specialised capabilities and support 
business expansion. For recruitment platforms, therefore, 
gross hiring demand is a more meaningful indicator than net 
employment creation alone. This structural characteristic 
contributes to the resilience of India’s organised recruitment 
market across economic cycles.
At the same time, AI is fundamentally reshaping the 
recruitment industry. Enterprises are increasingly adopting 
AI across candidate sourcing, screening, interview 
scheduling, matching, recruitment marketing and workforce 
planning. Rather than replacing recruitment platforms, 
AI is accelerating the industry’s transition towards more 
intelligent, automated and data -driven hiring processes, 
enabling recruiters to improve productivity while delivering 
better candidate experiences.
India’s position as a global technology and innovation 
hub continues to strengthen these structural trends. The 
country’s 2,100+ GCCs continue to expand hiring across 
engineering, product development, AI, cybersecurity and 
digital transformation. The employment landscape is also 
becoming more geographically diversified, with increasing 
investment across Tier II and Tier III cities creating new 
employment clusters. At the same time, the rapid growth 
of blue - and grey -collar segment and flexible workforce 
models is creating a large and underpenetrated opportunity 
for digital recruitment platforms serving the value segment.

The Indian Recruitment Model
India’s recruitment market is structurally different from most 
developed markets, and this distinction has been central 
to Naukri’s leadership in the country for over 20  years. 
In many global markets, recruitment is primarily driven 
by a job -posting model. Employers advertise vacancies, 
candidates submit applications, and recruiters evaluate 
the applicant pool. While this approach works efficiently in 
markets characterised by relatively balanced labour supply 
and demand, it becomes less effective in markets such as 
India, where a single vacancy can attract hundreds and in 
many cases, thousands of applications.
India’s recruitment ecosystem has therefore evolved 
around a database -led search model. Rather than relying 
solely on inbound applications, recruiters proactively The Indian Recruitment Model & Naukri’s Competitive Advantage
Platform Flywheel & Network Effects
This creates a powerful self -reinforcing platform flywheel. 
Unlike traditional recruitment businesses, where competitive 
advantages are primarily relationship -driven, digital 
recruitment platforms become stronger as participation 
increases. Every additional recruiter, candidate and 
interaction enhances the platform’s intelligence, improves 
matching quality and increases the value delivered to all 
participants. As these network effects compound over 
time, they become increasingly difficult for competitors 
to replicate.
Sales & Distribution Reach
These digital advantages are reinforced by one of the 
industry’s largest direct sales and customer engagement 
organisations. With a presence across more than 75 cities, 
the Company has built deep relationships with enterprises, 
recruitment consultants, GCCs, start -ups, and small and 
medium businesses, while simultaneously expanding its 
reach across Tier II and Tier III markets. This extensive 
market presence enables faster customer acquisition, 
stronger retention and deeper penetration across India’s 
organised recruitment market.CHART 7: NAUKRI FLYWHEEL
Database Scale, Freshness & Behavioural Data
Over nearly three decades, Naukri has built one of India’s 
largest and most dynamic recruitment ecosystems. As of 
March 31, 2026, the platform hosted 115 Million resumes, 
with approximately 23,000 new resumes added every day 
and more than 713,000 resumes updated daily during FY26, 
ensuring that recruiters have access to a continuously 
expanding and refreshed talent pool.Beyond scale, millions of daily interactions by recruiters 
and jobseekers generate rich behavioural signals 
that continually improve search relevance, candidate 
recommendations and matching accuracy. Supported by 
sustained investments in AI/ML, these proprietary datasets 
enable the platform to become increasingly intelligent 
over time.From Marketplace to Talent  
Solutions Platform
The Company’s strategy is also evolving beyond its 
traditional role as a recruitment marketplace. By integrating 
talent sourcing automation, talent intelligence, workflow 
management, skill assessment and candidate engagement 
capabilities into its ecosystem, Naukri is expanding from 
a hiring platform into a comprehensive talent solutions 
partner. These adjacent offerings deepen customer 
relationships, increase share of wallet and create multiple 
new avenues for monetisation while reinforcing the 
competitive strength of the core platform.
AI as Reinforcement, Not Disruption
AI represents the next phase of this evolution. Rather than 
disrupting the Company’s core business model, AI enhances 
the effectiveness of database -led recruitment by improving 
search quality, recommendation accuracy, recruiter 
productivity and candidate engagement. Backed by more 
than a decade of investments in AI, one of India’s largest 
applied AI labs comprising over 130 data science and ML 
professionals, and proprietary datasets that cannot be easily 
replicated, the Company believes it is well positioned to lead 
the next generation of technology -enabled recruitment.search candidate databases, identify relevant talent, and 
directly engage with prospective candidates. This approach 
significantly improves hiring efficiency by enabling 
recruiters to filter candidates based on skills, experience, 
location, compensation and other parameters before 
initiating contact.
As the recruitment process becomes increasingly 
search -led, the quality, scale and intelligence of candidate 
data become the principal sources of competitive 
advantage. Leadership in India’s recruitment market is 
determined not merely by the number of job listings or 
registered users, but by the ability to continuously enrich 
candidate data, generate superior matching outcomes and 
deliver measurable hiring efficiency for recruiters.Naukri

Candidate & Jobseeker Services (B2C)
This category focuses on the jobseeker side of the 
marketplace, deepening engagement with Naukri’s large 
existing user base through three offerings.
Naukri 360 is a comprehensive, largely self-serve do-it-
yourself (DIY) career platform offering specialised services 
for jobseekers, including resume preparation, interview 
training, and a range of mock interview and practice 
sessions. During FY26, the Company launched a Jobseeker 
Agent called Neo , which enables AI -powered job discovery, 
real-time job alerts and auto job apply (if enabled). Since 
April 2024, approximately 9.8 Million AI-powered resumes 
have been downloaded, and approximately 4.6 Million AI-
led interviews have been completed as of March 31, 2026.
Naukri 360 also carries a do-it-for-me (DIFM) layer, evolved 
from the original Naukri FastForward  service, in which a 
team of professional experts handle resume writing, profile 
building and related jobseeker support directly, creating a 
more bespoke, concierge-like experience for users. The 
DIY products and DIFM services complement each other, 
and as a result Naukri FastForward is progressively being 
folded into Naukri 360 as a premium, expert-led tier rather 
than existing as an independent sub-brand.
Naukri Minis  is a content platform that delivers curated, 
bite-sized updates on industry trends, job market insights, 
news and industry shifts and recruitment strategies. Naukri 
Minis hosts over 500,000 pieces of live content, generating 
1,500 hours of daily watch time.
The Naukri B2C business recorded 18.8% billings growth 
in FY26 while sustaining a high-margin, profitable model, 
with Q4 billings up 32.9%. Paid users rose from 1.3% to 
2.5% of the overall Naukri monthly active users over the 
last 15 months–a testimony to product adoption and 
value delivery. With deepening engagement, expanding 
monetisation levers and continued product innovation, the 
category is well positioned for faster growth.NaukriGulf
Beyond India, the Company operates a Middle East -focused 
online hiring platform, NaukriGulf , replicating Naukri’s 
successful Indian model in the region—starting with the 
Indian diaspora and expanding to diverse nationalities. 
This business is focused on the six GCC countries, with the 
UAE being the key market, followed by Saudi Arabia, Qatar, 
Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait. It has transformed into a leading 
regional hiring platform. The business witnessed strong 
activity through most of FY26, with a moderation in March 
owing to the West Asia conflict. Leveraging the region’s 
robust economic momentum, NaukriGulf delivered billings 
growth of 16.3% in FY26 while sustaining high operating 
profit margins. The business continues to deliver profitable 
growth, reflecting the depth and resilience of the Middle 
East recruitment market and providing a strong foundation 
for future expansion.
Job Hai
Hiring volumes in the value segment are growing rapidly 
across warehousing, logistics, manufacturing, delivery, retail 
and healthcare support, supported by sustained industrial 
activity and rapid urbanisation. However, the segment has 
distinct operating dynamics: digital penetration remains 
low, employers often hire urgently rather than periodically, 
workers typically do not maintain formal resumes, and job

AI as the Next Growth Multiplier
AI is reshaping every stage of the recruitment lifecycle—from 
candidate discovery and matching to recruiter productivity, 
workflows and talent intelligence. The Company believes 
AI represents one of the most significant long -term 
opportunities to enhance customer value, strengthen 
competitive differentiation and expand monetisation 
across its recruitment ecosystem.
The Company’s AI strategy extends well beyond 
improving productivity. By embedding AI across search, 
recommendations, job discovery, recruiter workflows and 
customer engagement, the Company is transforming Naukri 
from a recruitment marketplace into a comprehensive 
AI-enabled talent solutions platform. AI is also enabling 
the Company to broaden its participation across the 
recruitment value chain through an expanding portfolio of 
enterprise solutions, which deepen customer relationships, 
increase platform stickiness and diversify revenue streams 
beyond traditional recruitment subscriptions.
Backed by over a decade of investments in AI, one of India’s 
largest applied AI teams (over 130 data science and ML 
professionals), and proprietary behavioural datasets, the 
Company believes it is uniquely positioned to lead the 
next phase of AI -enabled recruitment. These investments 
are already translating into measurable outcomes, with 
productivity across multiple workflows improving by  
15–20% YoY.
Deepening Jobseeker Engagement 
& Monetisation
Alongside strengthening its enterprise offerings, the 
Company continues to invest in building deeper relationships 
with jobseekers throughout their career journeys. Its 
strategy extends beyond job discovery to helping users 
improve employability, navigate career transitions and 
make better career decisions.
The Company’s jobseeker ecosystem—Naukri 360, Naukri 
FastForward, Naukri Minis and Neo (jobseeker agent) 
offers services including resume enhancement, interview 
preparation, personalised job discovery, career guidance 
and curated content. As AI continues to make career 
services more personalised and interactive, the Company 
expects jobseeker engagement to become an increasingly 
important driver of user lifetime value, platform stickiness 
and long -term revenue diversification.Strategic Priorities and Outlook
Naukri’s long -term growth strategy is centred on expanding 
its leadership across India’s recruitment ecosystem while 
increasing customer value through technology, AI and 
product innovation. The Company believes that future 
growth will be driven not only by increase in hiring volumes, 
but also by expanding its share of recruitment spending, 
increasing monetisation across its customer base and 
broadening its participation across the end -to-end hiring 
lifecycle. The strategy is anchored on five complementary 
growth pillars.
Strengthening Leadership in the Core 
Recruitment Franchise
The mid -market recruitment segment (compensation 
levels of approximately ₹5–30 Lakh) remains the largest 
component of India’s organised white collar recruitment 
market and continues to be the foundation of the 
Company’s business. While hiring volumes in this segment 
are inherently linked to broader economic conditions, the 
long -term opportunity remains significant as recruitment 
continues to become increasingly organised and digital. 
The Company’s strategy is to deepen its leadership by 
expanding customer acquisition, increasing penetration 
among SMEs, strengthening its presence across Tier II 
and Tier III cities, and continuously enhancing recruiter 
productivity through AI -powered search, matching 
and talent sourcing automation. Alongside customer Scaling the Value Segment
India’s blue-and grey-collar workforce represents one of 
the country’s largest and fastest-growing employment 
segments. Increasing urbanisation, workforce formalisation 
and growth in logistics, manufacturing, retail, healthcare, 
hospitality and platform-based employment continue 
to expand long-term demand for organised hiring 
solutions. The Company is expanding its presence in the 
value segment beyond white-collar hiring, where Naukri 
already has a leading position. Its immediate priority is to 
strengthen Job Hai’s leadership in markets where it has 
established strong traction, while gradually expanding 
into additional metropolitan and large urban centres. Over 
the long term, continued formalisation of India’s labour 
market and increasing digital adoption are expected to 
create a significant opportunity for scalable platform-led 
recruitment in this segment.
Looking Ahead
The recruitment industry continues to evolve as enterprises 
increasingly adopt digital hiring, AI reshapes recruitment 
workflows and workforce mobility creates sustained 
demand for organised hiring solutions. Supported by 
market leadership, powerful network effects, trusted 
brands, proprietary data assets and continued investments 
in technology, the Company is well positioned to strengthen 
its competitive position, deepen customer relationships 
and expand its role across the recruitment value chain.
While hiring volumes may remain influenced by near -term 
macroeconomic conditions, the Company’s strategy 
remains focused on capturing a larger share of India’s 
long -term recruitment opportunity through innovation, 
disciplined execution and sustained investments in 
technology. Together, the Company’s five growth pillars 
position the recruitment business to sustain robust, 
profitable growth over the medium to long term.

Real Estate 
India’s real estate sector maintained strong momentum through FY26, underpinned by a 
resilient domestic economy amid global uncertainty. The office market scaled new highs as 
GCCs deepened their India operations and demand for Grade A assets remained strong. The 
residential market extended its post-pandemic upcycle, supported by increasing urbanisation, 
rising incomes and growing buyer appetite for higher-value homes. For 99acres, FY26 was 
marked by disciplined execution against its multi-year strategic transformation. The business 
progressed from being among the top three players to gaining leadership in traffic, reflecting 
sustained investments in customer experience, product and technology that translated into 
measurable market share gains.
Residential Real Estate Segment
The Indian residential real estate market sustained its 
post -pandemic momentum through CY25, marking a 
phase of stability and underlying resilience. Housing 
sales across the top eight cities stood at 0.35 Million 
units, with second -half volumes registering the highest 
half-yearly level recorded since the end of 2013. Demand 
remained well supported by the Reserve Bank of India’s 
cumulative 125 basis point reduction in the repo rate since 
February 2025, which aided affordability, along with eased 
financing conditions.
Buyer interest continued to gravitate towards higher -value 
homes. Sales of properties priced at I 10 Million and above 
grew 14% YoY  and now constitute half of total annual sales, 
with premium segments such as I 20–500 Million recording 
even sharper growth. Residential launches reached  
0.36 Million units, the second -highest annual volume since 
2014, as developers calibrated the pace of new supply to 
keep pipelines aligned with demand.New supply remained concentrated in higher ticket sizes, 
reflecting the continued shift in the market’s composition 
towards premium housing. Strong price escalation 
followed, with NCR, Hyderabad and Bengaluru recording 
price growth of 19%, 13% and 12% YoY respectively, driven 
largely by the strong focus on premium and high-rise 
residential developments.
Inventory levels are best assessed alongside sales velocity. 
The quarters -to-sell metric–the number of quarters required 
to clear existing inventory at the trailing eight -quarter sales 
pace–held broadly steady at around 5.8 quarters (under 
eighteen months) across the eight markets, indicating 
that the overall market fundamentals remained healthy. 
Developers increasingly relied on buyer- centric measures 
such as flexible financing structures, subvention schemes 
and selective stamp duty waivers to support transaction 
sales momentum.
